articles.title: The next export story: A $50 billion prize India can't afford to miss
articles.summary: India's telecom equipment industry is a minor global player, with annual exports of only $0.6-1 billion. Imports significantly outstrip exports by four to five times, indicating a major trade imbalance and reliance on foreign technology. This highlights an opportunity for bolstering domestic manufacturing and achieving greater self-sufficiency in a vital technological sector.

articles.title: In 2021, Johnston Atoll eradicated invasive yellow crazy ants after an 11-year effort; the refuge is home to nearly 13,000 red-tailed tropicbird nesting pairs
articles.summary: Johnston Atoll successfully eradicated invasive yellow crazy ants after an 11-year effort, safeguarding its unique ecosystem, including nearly 13,000 red-tailed tropicbirds. This long-term ecological restoration showcases dedicated environmental stewardship and the impact of sustained conservation initiatives on protecting critical biodiversity in remote refuges. It underscores the importance of persistent efforts in preserving fragile environments.

articles.title: Northeast India looks to emerge as space-tech gateway to Southeast Asia
articles.summary: The Space Industry Association of India (SIA-India) and NESAC are organizing the Northeast India Space Workshop 2026 in Guwahati. This initiative aims to explore and promote space applications within the Northeast region. For SSB aspirants, this highlights India's focus on regional development through technology, enhancing national capabilities in space science, and fostering innovation, crucial for security and progress.

articles.title: In 2021, scientists reported that Sydney cockatoos had learned to pry open garbage bins; by the end of 2019, the trick had spread across 44 suburbs
articles.summary: Scientists reported in 2021 that Sydney cockatoos developed a clever method to pry open garbage bins. This innovative behavior, observed spreading among the bird population since late 2019, showcases remarkable animal learning and social transmission of skills. It offers insights into avian intelligence and adaptability, becoming a notable instance of cultural evolution in the animal kingdom.

articles.title: DELIVERY OF MANGROL - THE THIRD ANTI-SUBMARINE WARFARE SHALLOW WATER CRAFT BUILT BY CSL, KOCHI
articles.summary: Mangrol, the third Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft (ASW SWC), is being constructed by Cochin Shipyard Limited for the Indian Navy. This vessel signifies a crucial step in bolstering India's coastal defence capabilities against submarine threats. Its development underscores the nation's ongoing commitment to indigenous defence production and modernizing its naval fleet to ensure maritime security in shallow waters.
